elements.element: No minimum purchase / take-or-pay / volume commitment imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer has no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, or volume commitment."

elements.element: Fees payable only for services ordered or usage actually consumed
elements.evidence: "Customer pays only for Services ordered under a signed Order Form and, where an Order Form provides usage-based pricing, actually used."

elements.element: Original three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay obligation removed
elements.evidence: replace of "commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis"

elements.element: Commitment expressly limited to the current 12-month term
elements.evidence: clause contains no commitment period; "has no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, or volume commitment"
no reduction-on-notice mechanic appears in the rendered clause

elements.element: Shortfall handled by true-up rather than penalty
elements.evidence: no true-up or shortfall language in the rendered clause

reasons: The locked preferred level is fully achieved: the take-or-pay minimum is deleted and replaced with an express no-minimum statement plus payment for ordered/actually-used Services only, matching "No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only."

Fallback elements (12-month limit, 30-day reduction, true-up) are absent, but the fallback is a separate, lesser bargain and is correctly left to the margin comment rather than mixed into the operative text.

The rewrite is confined to the single offending sentence in 2.1; because the entire operative obligation was the take-or-pay commitment, no operator, number, or short phrase could cure it, so the sentence-level replacement is the minimum necessary. The official ratio gate failure reflects sentence length, not surplus concessions or added rights.

No free-standing reduction or termination rights, exceptions, or new defined terms were introduced; Sec 12.3 and the definitions of Order Form and Services remain intact and consistent with the new 2.1.
